title: HR: Failed Logins on Inactive Accounts

transcript.speaker: HR Admin
transcript.text: AOC, this is HR. We're getting a spike in Account Locked alerts for six employees who aren't scheduled today. They're not on site, not using any systems. Their accounts keep getting hit with failed login attempts—passwords are being tried repeatedly. Is there a system-wide authentication issue?

transcript.speaker: AOC Duty Officer
transcript.text: Hold on, HR—this is the AOC. We’re not seeing any active network anomalies. Is it possible someone's testing credentials from outside?

transcript.speaker: HR Admin
transcript.text: No, it's not external. The failed attempts are coming from internal IP 10.66.0.50, which is assigned to NCIA-PACS-CORE. That host is not supposed to be initiating auth requests. We’ve already disabled the accounts. But the pattern's consistent—each account is being targeted with a different password set, then locked out.

transcript.speaker: AOC Duty Officer
transcript.text: Understood. We’ll check the PACS logs and notify IT. Thanks for the alert.

instructorNote: This inject introduces credential-spray behavior from the rogue device. Watch for IT to check auth logs on NCIA-PACS-CORE and Security to validate the source IP.
